title: Unbreakable
description: Tie a knot and find out whether it is one. The rope is real — a Verlet chain that cannot pass through itself — and you author every crossing yourself with an OVER/UNDER switch. Then close it into a loop, the way a rakhi is a loop, and watch it tighten: a rope that was never knotted collapses into a clean ring, and a real knot jams against its own thickness and stops. That is the proof, not an animation of one. Whatever survives gets read off the rope as a Gauss code, reduced by Reidemeister moves, and named — the unknot, the trefoil, the figure-eight, the cinquefoil, the three-twist. Most crossings that will not come out goes to the leaderboard.
